summary: 19 hand mutations of `Invariants.checkChain` run against the full :sequencer:test suite in an issued review tree; 14 killed, 5 survived and none of the survivors changes a verdict. The rename I4 -> `order` is pinned by mutation (renaming it back is killed by 5 fixtures). The eight fixtures' reds are genuine assertion failures at the assertion line numbers the current file has. `aPermutationThatALSOOverlapsReportsBOTHNames` is pinned in BOTH directions: dropping I2 for a permuted stream and dropping `order` for an overlapping stream are each killed by that fixture alone. No existing assertion was weakened -- containsExactly("I4") -> containsExactly("order") is the same strength.

findings.title: Two javadoc blocks still name I4 for an arm that now reports `order`
findings.failure_scenario: Line 217 reads "RB is well-ordered, so exactly one I4 must be reported and it must name RA" while the assertion four lines down (line 238) asserts "order"; line 247 reads "calling it I4 as well would report one defect under two names" while the same test's .as() message on line 264 was updated to `order`. checkChain no longer emits I4 from any arm -- grep of sequencer/src shows the only I4 producer is ReaderInvariants' DROP clause. The failure this invites is the doc-to-test-to-production inversion: a maintainer reconciling the test with its own javadoc changes the assertion to "I4", and then production to satisfy it -- reinstating exactly the overclaim this row removed. No verdict is wrong today; the assertions and .as() messages are all correct.
findings.mutation: Not a surviving mutation -- the NAME is pinned. MEASURED: renaming the Violation back to new Violation("I4", ...) is KILLED by aBatchedDeltaWhoseSECONDSegmentREWINDSIsStillCaught, aStreamOutOfOrderTWICEIsStillONEViolation, aStreamOutOfOrderOnlyInALATERPairIsStillCaught, ONEStreamPermutedInABatchDoesNotIndictTheOTHER and aPermutationThatALSOOverlapsReportsBOTHNames. The defect is prose-only, hence minor.

findings.title: The `order` violation's detail string is unpinned except for the stream key
findings.failure_scenario: The diff rewrites this detail message and attaches a comment justifying the rewrite ("NO SEGMENT INDEX IN THE MESSAGE: `r` walks this STREAM's runs, not the delta's segments, and a single-segment delta with two runs of one stream reported 'segment 1' where no segment 1 exists"). Nothing asserts the new wording, the sequence number or the two offsets. The only detail assertion in the suite is ONEStreamPermutedInABatchDoesNotIndictTheOTHER's contains(RA)/doesNotContain(RB). So the message a human reads when the 1,000-seed sweep of M4.13 fails can name the wrong chain entry, or report the offsets backwards, and the suite stays green -- the diagnostic points the reader at the wrong delta while the verdict itself stays right. Minor because no invariant name and no violation count changes.
findings.mutation: THREE MEASURED SURVIVORS against the full :sequencer:test suite: (1) `+ e.sequence() +` -> `+ 0L +` (every `order` violation claims sequence 0) SURVIVED; (2) swapping the two offsets in the message -- `inSegmentOrder.get(r)` and `get(r - 1)` exchanged in the string only -- SURVIVED, so "a run starting at 4 follows one starting at 0" is reported for the reverse fact; (3) restoring the exact pre-diff wording `": segment " + r + " starts at " ... " after "` -- the mislabel the comment says was fixed -- SURVIVED. Two further survivors are equivalent rather than gaps: LinkedHashMap -> HashMap (only reorders the returned list, which no test pins and no caller specifies), and guarding the order arm with `delta.segments().size() > 1` (CommitLog.commitSubmissions builds runs from a Map<RunKey,Long> per segment, so a single-segment delta cannot carry two runs of one stream).
